name: Convoy of Hope
summary: A faith-based humanitarian charity based in Springfield, Missouri, that passes donated food, clothing, household goods and medicines to partner churches and charities in the US and abroad, feeds 635,000 children a school-day meal in poor countries, trains farmers and women, holds community events in US cities, and sends relief supplies to US and overseas disasters. Over four fifths of its expenses are donated goods, booked at the donors' wholesale values.

spending.source: https://convoyofhope.org/financials/ (Convoy-of-Hope-Financial-Statements-BMWL-2023-2024.pdf, consolidated financial statements for the year to 31 December 2024, audited by Batts Morrison Wales & Lee, statement of activities p. 5 and note K p. 14): programme expenses $598,182k as reported, of which $531,950k were donated goods distributed; Convoy's own (cash) programme spending $66,232k.

lines.label: Partner resourcing, community development, community events and disaster response
lines.source: https://convoyofhope.org/financials/ (Convoy-of-Hope-Financial-Statements-BMWL-2023-2024.pdf, note K p. 14, 2024): each programme's expenses less its gifts in kind: partner resourcing $338,088k less $326,557k = $11,531k, community development $121,209k less $84,374k = $36,835k, community events $72,333k less $68,589k = $3,744k, disaster response $66,552k less $52,430k = $14,122k. One line because charityevals models all four as branches of one humanitarian-relief model. Weights are cash, the money donations pay for: donated goods enter the model's credit share, not its cost.
